baseline: Tenseien does not offer a dinner buffet at 16:15; dinner service begins at 17:30 (lunch ends at 14:30), leaving insufficient time before the 18:15 Kenban arrival.
Tamura Ginkatsutei does not accept reservations and routinely has 45–90 minute waits on Sunday afternoons; seating a walk-in group of 8 between 13:05 and 14:25 is highly improbable.
Day 2 features extreme geographical ping-ponging: Gora -> Sengokuhara (Glass no Mori & A-Coop) -> Gora again (Gora Brewery) -> Miyanoshita (Funny's) -> Sengokuhara.
Leaving A-Coop at 17:55, taking taxis to drop groceries at the villa, and arriving in Gora for an 18:30 table is mathematically unfeasible on winding mountain roads.
Under Japan's Fueiho (Entertainment Business Act), Round1 arcade floors must close by 24:00, meaning only bowling and karaoke remain accessible late night.
variant: Hatsuhana Soba's Shinkan branch permanently closed in December 2021; only the renewed main building (Honten) operates by the river.

A 1-minute transfer from the Tokaido Shinkansen gates to the Osaka Metro Midosuji Line at Shin-Osaka (arriving 21:20, boarding 21:21) is physically impossible for a group of 8 with luggage (requires at least 7–10 minutes).
Day 1 involves heavy backtracking: ascending to Sengokuhara at 14:30, descending back to Yumoto at 18:30 for Furatto Geisha, then ascending again to Sengokuhara at 20:45.

gemini.summary: Itinerary A is clearly superior. Itinerary B collapses on Day 2 with irrational geographical ping-ponging across the mountain (Gora to Sengokuhara and immediately back to Gora for dinner) and schedules an unreservable Sunday peak lunch at Tamura Ginkatsutei that would derail the entire afternoon. While Itinerary A requires an expensive taxi detour on Saturday evening to accommodate both Sengokuhara sightseeing and the Yumoto geisha show, its Day 2 and Day 3 routings are smooth, logical, and supported by accurate booking requirements and dishes.

specificity.why: A gives more hard detail: phone numbers, menu items with prices, per-room bath rates, exact metro departures and a dated to-do list. B is concrete but lighter on prices, for example 'priced at booking' for Tenseien and 'per-game prices' at Round1.

accuracy.why: A correctly flags the 1 Nov 2026 refund-based tax-free change, which B misses. But A contradicts itself: it says goods are no longer sealed, then tells you to keep the outlet bags sealed. It also lists a ¥160 Tozan fare that the Freepass already covers, and gives the Yuryo shuttle as 5 min one way and 13 min back. B's slips are smaller: a 105-min Romancecar slot (about 85 min is normal), a 20-min pier-to-shrine walk (about 10 min), and a MONTA session that may exceed a 2-hour December cap. Both assume a 09:00 first ropeway car, when winter starts may be later.

feasibility.why: A's Day 1 ping-pongs by taxi Yumoto→Sengokuhara→Yumoto→Sengokuhara: three long two-car rides costing tens of thousands of yen. Its Shin-Osaka plan relies on a 1-minute shinkansen-to-metro connection. Its luggage plan is muddled: bags are 'forwarded to Osaka', then ride in taxis all day through the outlets. B does everything in Yumoto before one trip up and runs a coherent TA-Q-BIN chain with overnight bags. B's risks are the Tamura queue against its 14:30 lunch cutoff and a three-hour MONTA stay.

fit.why: Both suit 20-year-olds: geisha drinking games, brewpub, burgers, villa onsen nights and Round1. B adds an all-you-can-drink buffet and a cheap tofu-katsu lunch, which suits the group's budget and vibe better. A's ¥3,300–15,000 Nobu lunch is a splurge, and A fits in a Dotonbori bar crawl before Round1.

sourcing.why: Both cite similar mixes of official sites, Google reviews, Reddit and blogs. Many logistics stops in both are unsourced, including the shinkansen, villa and Round1 entries.

usefulness.why: A packs more information, but its routing and logistics errors would cost real money and stress. B is the more reliable plan to follow, though it misses the new tax-free refund rules.

baseline: Romancecar slot of 08:40–10:25 is too long; the ride is about 85 min.
Motohakone pier to Hakone Shrine is given as about 20 min; it is closer to 10.
MONTA is planned for 20:35–00:00 and relies on a pickup that may not run in that window or allow stays that long in December.
Tamura Ginkatsutei lunch starts at 13:05 with an admitted 30–60 min Sunday wait against a 14:30 cutoff, which is risky.
Misses the 1 Nov 2026 shift to refund-based tax-free shopping.
Villa drinks bought in Yumoto at 14:15 get carried through the buffet and the geisha show.
Hikari ride length and the arrival time 'just before 21:00' are optimistic for a 18:50 departure.
variant: Day 1 routing sends two taxis up and down the mountain three times (Yumoto→Sengokuhara→Yumoto→Sengokuhara), which is very expensive and inefficient.
Shinkansen arrives at Shin-Osaka at 21:20, but the plan has the metro leaving at 21:21, a 1-minute connection.
Contradiction: 'goods are no longer sealed' under the refund system, yet 'leave the outlet bags sealed for the tax-free rules anyway'.
Luggage plan is inconsistent: Day 1 assumes suitcases may already be forwarded to Osaka, while Day 3 has the bags riding in taxis all day through the outlets and Tokinosumika.
Gives the Gora→Miyanoshita Tozan train as a ¥160 budget option, but that leg is covered by the Freepass they already hold.
Yuryo shuttle is given as about 5 min out and 13 min back.
Kujō check-in runs 21:50–22:05 while the onward train departs at 22:04. The ride is also given as both 18 min and about 23 min door to door.
The MONTA slot (21:25–23:30) slightly exceeds the stated 2-hour December cap.
Describes the 20 Dec light as 'late-winter', and the Romancecar view as rice fields as the scenery turns green, which reads oddly for December.
The tax-free [BRING] passport block is duplicated.

judge.summary: A is more detailed and catches the 2026 tax-free change, but its Day 1 taxi shuttling, its 1-minute Shin-Osaka connection and its contradictory luggage and sealed-bag advice make it less reliable. B's routing is more logical, keeping Yumoto activities together and running a clean TA-Q-BIN chain, and its errors are minor timing estimates. B is the better guide to actually follow.
